Manipulator Mechanics and Control Chapter 14. Control Architecture 01 Control Architecture Overview Control architecture defines the organizational structure through which a robotic manipulator converts high-level objectives into coordinated physical actions. It establishes relationships among task planning, motion generation, feedback regulation, actuator commands, and safety supervision. A well-designed architecture separates responsibilities while maintaining reliable communication across components operating at different computational speeds.
articles.author: Richard Minsoo Go

articles.body: STATERA Library · Series 03 · Volume 02 · Chapter 13 · EN Source: https://github.com/Statera-Library/03_Vol_02_Manipulator_Mechanics_and_Control/blob/main/Chapter_13_Workspace_Optimization/Chapter_13_Workspace_Optimization_EN.md Volume 02. Manipulator Mechanics and Control Chapter 13. Workspace Optimization 01 Workspace Analysis Workspace analysis is a fundamental process in manipulator engineering that determines the spatial regions a robot can reach and operate within effectively. It provides the geometric and kinematic foundation for evaluating robot configurations, selecting installation positions, and planning manipulation tasks. In mobile manipulators, workspace analysis must consider both the articulated robot arm and the movable base.

Manipulator Mechanics and Control Chapter 12. Collision Detection 01 Collision Detection Overview Collision detection is a fundamental capability in robotic manipulation systems, enabling robots to identify, predict, and respond to physical interactions with surrounding objects, equipment, and humans. It provides the foundation for safe motion planning, reliable task execution, and damage prevention.
articles.author: Richard Minsoo Go

articles.body: STATERA Library · Series 03 · Volume 02 · Chapter 11 · EN Source: https://github.com/Statera-Library/03_Vol_02_Manipulator_Mechanics_and_Control/blob/main/Chapter_11_Grippers/Chapter_11_Grippers_EN.md Volume 02. Manipulator Mechanics and Control Chapter 11. Grippers 01 Gripper Design Gripper design is a fundamental discipline in robotic manipulation because the gripper establishes the physical interface between a robot and the objects it handles. A successful design must provide reliable grasping, controlled release, and sufficient adaptability to different object geometries. In mobile manipulators, gripper performance also influences arm dynamics, positioning accuracy, operational safety, and overall task efficiency.
articles.author: Richard Minsoo Go

articles.title: How to Batch Rewrite 100+ JPEGs and PNGs to 300 DPI in Your Browser (Zero Re-encoding, One ZIP)
articles.excerpt: Print shops, photographers delivering wedding galleries, and Etsy printable sellers run into the same repetitive workflow bottleneck every week: a folder of 60 to 150 high-resolution JPEGs or PNGs get…
articles.body: Print shops, photographers delivering wedding galleries, and Etsy printable sellers run into the same repetitive workflow bottleneck every week: a folder of 60 to 150 high-resolution JPEGs or PNGs gets flagged by preflight software because every file is tagged 72 DPI or 96 DPI instead of 300 DPI . Opening 80 images one by one in Photoshop just to uncheck Resample and type 300 is slow, and running them through naive "online DPI converter" scripts introduces two subtle bugs that break real print delivery. Bug 1: Re-encoding JPEG Scan Data Ruins Quality Many quick web tools "change DPI" by decoding the image onto a <canvas> element and exporting a fresh JPEG.
articles.author: Casey Marlin

articles.excerpt: STATERA Library · Series 03 · Volume 02 · Chapter 10 · EN https://github.com/Statera-Library/03_Vol_02_Manipulator_Mechanics_and_Control/blob/main/Chapter_10_End_Effectors/Chapter_10_End_Effectors_EN.…
articles.body: STATERA Library · Series 03 · Volume 02 · Chapter 10 · EN Source: https://github.com/Statera-Library/03_Vol_02_Manipulator_Mechanics_and_Control/blob/main/Chapter_10_End_Effectors/Chapter_10_End_Effectors_EN.md Volume 02. Manipulator Mechanics and Control Chapter 10. End Effectors 01 End Effector Overview An end effector is the functional device mounted at the terminal interface of a robotic manipulator, enabling the robot to interact directly with objects, tools, and surrounding environments. While the robot arm provides positioning and orientation capabilities, the end effector performs the actual physical operation. Its design determines how effectively the robotic system can grasp, hold, move, process, or manipulate objects during industrial and service tasks.
articles.author: Richard Minsoo Go

articles.title: Manipulator Mechanics and Control — Ch.09: Compliance Control [EN]
articles.excerpt: STATERA Library · Series 03 · Volume 02 · Chapter 09 · EN https://github.com/Statera-Library/03_Vol_02_Manipulator_Mechanics_and_Control/blob/main/Chapter_09_Compliance_Control/Chapter_09_Compliance_C…
articles.body: STATERA Library · Series 03 · Volume 02 · Chapter 09 · EN Source: https://github.com/Statera-Library/03_Vol_02_Manipulator_Mechanics_and_Control/blob/main/Chapter_09_Compliance_Control/Chapter_09_Compliance_Control_EN.md Volume 02. Manipulator Mechanics and Control Chapter 09. Compliance Control 01 Compliance Control Overview Compliance control is a fundamental approach in robotic manipulation that enables a robot to respond flexibly to external forces, physical contact, and environmental uncertainty. Unlike rigid position control, which attempts to maintain a predetermined trajectory, compliance control allows controlled deviations from the commanded motion.
articles.author: Richard Minsoo Go

articles.excerpt: Malware cocktail delivers cryptocurrency theft payloads and iOS exploits, among other things.
articles.body: Hundreds of websites using the Optimizely website personalization platform served unsuspecting visitors a potent malware cocktail that targeted cryptocurrency wallets, stole payment card data, cookies, and screenshots, and delivered exploit kits for infecting iPhones and iPads, researchers said Tuesday. ReportURI said it identified 178 websites—including CNN, Zoom, the BBC, and Salesforce—that were affected. JavaScript digitally signed by Optimizely and then loaded into customer pages had been modified to include malicious components that attempted to infect visitor devices with multiple payloads. When wares were installed successfully, they swapped user cryptocurrency wallet addresses for the attackers.

articles.title: NASA's Voyager 1 launched second, so how did it beat Voyager 2 to a light-day by nearly a decade?
articles.excerpt: Voyager 1 just reached a light-day in space, but Voyager 2 won't do the same until 2035, due to speed choices made throughout their 50-year missions.
articles.body: Voyager 1 is about to reach a light-day of distance in space, but Voyager 2 won't hit the mark until about 2035. Why the big difference? On Nov. 18, Voyager 1 will be so far away from Earth that it will take a full light-day (24 hours) to send a signal to the distant spacecraft, at 16,094,799,096 miles (25,902,068,356 kilometers). Since light is essentially the maximum speed in the universe (absent using devices like wormholes, or quantum-physics puzzles), it's a big deal — so big that NASA will be celebrating the milestone by asking fans to shine Morse Code signals at the sky. But why will Voyager 2 take nearly a decade longer?
articles.author: Elizabeth Howell

articles.body: 2 min read NASA Space Apps Challenge Breaks Global Hackathon Records Two NASA Space Apps Challenge participants in Vilhena, Brazil work together during the annual hackathon on their project submission. NASA On Nov. 14 and 15, NASA held the annual Space Apps Challenge with a record-breaking 181,835 registered participants taking part in 593 events around the world. The annual hackathon invites participants to use NASA’s open data to address one of 14 challenges focused on space exploration or Earth science. This year, the hackathon drew 59% more registrants and was the 5th year in a row with increased participation. Since 2012, NASA Space Apps Challenge has hosted the two-day event, which has included more than 600,000 people from more than 190 countries.

articles.title: Space is filling up with junk. Could laser-reflecting mirrors help humanity clean things up?
articles.excerpt: The British company Foundational thinks its laser-reflecting tech can help humanity fight the space-junk problem — and it just proved out a demo version in an orbital test.
articles.body: A British startup thinks it can help humanity deal with its space junk problem. Millions of pieces of space debris circle Earth at the moment, according to the European Space Agency (ESA). Even the smallest fragments are potentially dangerous, given how fast stuff travels in orbit. Experts have proposed a range of measures to deal with this junk. The smallest bits, for example, may require big space nets, or lasering the stuff down to Earth. Large satellites are increasingly being deliberately deorbited these days, and a few have even been refueled to keep them operating in orbit — something that will likely start happening more and more over the coming years. Now, the British startup Foundational has another idea to throw into the mix: retroreflectors.

articles.body: 4 Min Read New Album of Baby Star Sounds Shared by NASA’s Chandra A new album from NASA’s Chandra X-ray Observatory collects snapshots of baby stars across the galaxy and beyond and transforms that data into sound. Four new sonifications use data of stars that are actively forming, captured by Chandra and other NASA telescopes By studying places in the universe where stars are currently being born and young stars are present, astronomers can better understand the lifecycle of all stars, including our own Sun. articles.title: 'Neuromancer:' Release date, cast & everything we know about Apple TV's new cyberpunk series
articles.excerpt: Hack into our handy guide to this electrifying adaptation of William Gibson’s cult ‘80s novel.
articles.body: We're in a bit of a cyberpunk revival at the moment. 2026 gave the excellent second season of Netflix’s "Cyberpunk: Edgerunners," and Prime Video's " Blade Runner 2099 " is just around the corner. 2027 will continue this trend with " Neuromancer " blasting onto Apple TV. Based on cyberspace guru William Gibson’s seminal 1984 novel, "Neuromancer" follows Case, a brilliant hacker who falls into a web of digital espionage and crime as he attempts an impossible corporate heist. The pulp noir novel has been hailed as a generational revelation, and its slang and terminology have become ingrained in computer nerd subcultures.
